[RFCS.16.4] The fast lane is **not** a fourth disposition — it is the inject band's
1-byte sub-range. Inject atoms are allocated low-to-high, so the first fifteen fall in
`1–15` (1-byte). The inject atoms take `FactAssert`=1, `FactRetract`=2,
`ClockAdvance`=3 (the structurally-hottest stream atoms — one per fact/clock event on an
unbounded stream); `4–15` are reserved for future inject atoms (1-byte for free), and any
inject atom beyond fifteen overflows to `16–127` (2-byte). The inject set is structurally
small, so overflow is unlikely.
